segments.en: Hello English learners, welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 您好英语学习者，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
And I'm Erica.
And today we have a fun and scary dialogue.
segments.zh: 今天我们有一个有趣而可怕的对话。

segments.en: That's right.
This lesson is full of language you can use to talk about being scared.
segments.zh: 这节课充满了你可以用来谈论害怕的语言。

segments.en: Alright, so we're gonna be looking at a scary lesson today and we have nothing to preview so let's listen to this dialogue and see why everyone is so scared.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们今天要看一个可怕的课程，我们没有什么可预览的，所以让我们听听这个对话，看看为什么每个人都这么害怕。

segments.en: Hey, why are we at this scary looking mansion?
segments.zh: 我们怎么跑到这座阴森森的大宅来了？

segments.en: It's like ultra spooky.
I told you already Shabby.
segments.zh: 我不是早跟你说了嘛，沙比。

segments.en: The owner of the house says there's a ghost haunting his house.
So we have to go in and investigate.
I don't like this.
Come on guys, stop being such cowards.
It's a mystery and an adventure.
segments.zh: 这可是个神秘又刺激的冒险。

segments.en: This place gives me the creeps.
Seriously guys, let's get out of here.
I'm getting goosebumps just being here.
segments.zh: 我光站在这儿就起鸡皮疙瘩。

segments.en: Shabby is a scaredy cat.
That laugh came from this room.
segments.zh: 那个笑声来自这个房间。

segments.en: Let's go and check it out.
Look, a ghost!
Run!
Well, that sounds really scary but actually it kind of reminds me of another TV show.
segments.zh: 嗯，这听起来真的很可怕，但实际上它让我想起了另一个电视节目。

segments.en: Very similar to another TV show but it's different.
segments.zh: 与另一个电视节目非常相似，但它是不同的。

segments.en: Okay, but some interesting language that you can use to talk about things that are scary so why don't we look at that now in Language Takeaway.

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
So let's start with the very first line of our dialogue.
segments.zh: 因此，让我们从对话的第一行开始。

segments.en: Shabby described the mansion to be ultra spooky.
segments.zh: Shabby 将这座豪宅描述为超级恐怖。

segments.en: It's ultra spooky.
Spooky.
So, okay, we've got two interesting words here, ultra and spooky.
segments.zh: 所以，好吧，我们这里有两个有趣的词，Ultra 和 Spooky。

segments.en: Now spooky is scary, right?
It's a little bit scary.
It maybe makes you feel a little bit uncomfortable or maybe it makes you feel a little bit scared.
segments.zh: 它可能会让你感到有点不舒服，或者它可能会让你感到有点害怕。

segments.en: Okay, so not very scared.
Not super scared.
But ultra spooky.
So ultra is another way of saying super or very or really spooky.
segments.zh: 所以 Ultra 是另一种表达超级或非常或真正令人毛骨悚然的方式。

segments.en: So if it's ultra spooky then it's...
segments.zh: 所以如果它是极端恐怖的，那它是...

segments.en: Very scary.
Okay.
All right, so our next word.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们的下一个词。

segments.en: They said that in the house there is a ghost haunting the house.
segments.zh: 他们说房子里有一个鬼魂出没。

segments.en: Okay, there is a ghost haunting his house.
segments.zh: 好吧，有个鬼魂在他家里出没。

segments.en: Okay, so the verb to haunt.
Okay, to haunt.
So the ghost is coming to the house frequently and not letting them live in peace.
segments.zh: 所以鬼经常来家里，不让他们安静地生活。

segments.en: When a ghost haunts something, it visits it often and scares it.
segments.zh: 当鬼魂出没时，它经常拜访它并吓到它。

segments.en: Exactly.
Now, they were all afraid and they didn't want to go in and so Wilma called everyone cowards.
segments.zh: 现在，他们都害怕，他们不想进去，所以威尔玛称每个人都胆怯。

segments.en: Stop being such cowards.
Cowards.
So, a coward.
A coward is a person that's not brave.
segments.zh: 懦夫是一个不勇敢的人。

segments.en: A person who's scared of everything.
Exactly.
So, they were being cowards.
They were afraid so that's why they didn't want to go in.
segments.zh: 他们很害怕，所以他们不想进去。

segments.en: Well, speaking of being afraid, Shabby said, I'm getting goose bumps.
segments.zh: 好吧，说到害怕，Shabby 说，我开始起鸡皮疙瘩。

segments.en: Goose bumps.
To get goose bumps.
All right, to get goose bumps.
segments.zh: 好吧，to get goose bumps，起鸡皮疙瘩。

segments.en: Now, goose bumps, it may sound a little bit strange but it's very easy when you're scared or maybe you're cold, the skin on your arms or on your back, it gets a little bit bumpy.
segments.zh: 现在，goose bumps 听起来可能有点怪，但道理很简单：当你害怕或者觉得冷时，手臂或后背的皮肤会起小疙瘩。

segments.en: So your skin looks like chicken skin.
segments.zh: 所以你的皮肤看起来像鸡皮。

segments.en: Exactly, chicken skin and that's actually how we call it in Spanish, chicken skin but this is goose bumps so I guess it's kind of similar.
segments.zh: 确切地说，就是鸡皮；西班牙语里我们就是这么叫的，也是鸡皮，不过这里是 goose bumps，我想两者挺像的。

segments.en: A goose.
Yeah, same idea.
Goose bumps.
All right and finally, Scruffy said, Shabby is a scaredy cat.
segments.zh: 好吧，最后，Scruffy 说，Shabby 是个胆小鬼。

segments.en: A scaredy cat.
A scaredy cat.
You're a scaredy cat.
Well, a scaredy cat is not really a cat, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，scaredy cat 其实不是猫，对吧？

segments.en: No, no, no.
It's a person who's afraid of everything.
segments.zh: 这是一个害怕一切的人。

segments.en: Okay.
Similar to a coward.
But more informal.
Much more informal.
So somebody is a scaredy cat and I think even a little bit more juvenile.
segments.zh: 所以 scaredy cat 就是形容某个人，我觉得还更幼稚一些。

segments.en: As adults.
So children use it.
Yeah, as adults, you wouldn't say he's a scaredy cat.
segments.zh: 是的，作为成年人，你不会说他是一只害怕的猫。

segments.en: All right, great.
So some interesting scary language.
segments.zh: 所以一些有趣的可怕语言。

I told you already, Shabby.

I don't like this.

Seriously, guys.

segments.en: Shabby is a scaredy cat.

Run.

So a scary looking mansion.
Okay, so the mansion looks scary.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这座豪宅看起来很可怕。

segments.en: That looks very scary.
Now this is a really useful and helpful pattern you can use with English.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常实用的句型，在英语里很有用。

segments.en: Something looking.
So adjective looking.
Right, so you can say good looking.
segments.zh: 对，比如你可以说 good looking。

segments.zh: 还有很多例子，所以我们现在为什么不听更多。

segments.en: Example one.
That guy is making me nervous.
He's really creepy looking.
segments.zh: 他看起来真的很毛骨悚然。

segments.en: Example two.
I saw the craziest looking house today.
segments.zh: 我今天看到了看起来最疯狂的房子。

segments.en: It was built upside down.
Example three.
What a nice looking dog.
Can I pet him?

segments.zh: 好吧，很好的例子，现在我们知道怎么把 looking 和不同的形容词搭配了。

segments.zh: 对于我们的下一个短语，Shabby 说这个地方让我毛骨悚然。

segments.en: All right, gives me the creeps.
To give someone the creeps.
So if something gives you the creeps.
segments.zh: 所以如果有什么东西让你毛骨悚然。

segments.en: It makes you feel uncomfortable and scared.
segments.zh: 它让你感到不舒服和害怕。

segments.en: Maybe scared, maybe nervous.
Okay, so why don't we give some examples.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们为什么不举一些例子。

segments.en: I could say, hey Marco, see that guy over there?
segments.zh: 我可以说，嘿，马可，看到那边的那个人了吗？

segments.en: He keeps looking at me.
He's giving me the creeps.
Okay, or I can say clowns give me the creeps.
segments.zh: 好吧，或者我可以说小丑让我毛骨悚然。

segments.en: Oh, that's right.
You're afraid of clowns.
I am afraid of clowns.
They give me the creeps.
All right, well, it's a really helpful, useful phrase to use when you're talking about being afraid.
segments.zh: 好吧，当你谈论害怕时，这是一个非常有用、有用的短语。

I told you already shabby.

segments.en: So what do you think, Erica?
Do you believe in ghosts?
Have you ever seen a ghost?
No, I totally do not believe in ghosts.
But I understand that you disagree with me.
segments.zh: 但我知道你不同意我的观点。

segments.en: Well, I've experienced strange things, but I don't know if it was a ghost or an alien.
segments.zh: 好吧，我经历过奇怪的事情，但我不知道是鬼还是外星人。

segments.en: I don't know.
It could have been anything.
An alien?
An invisible alien.
Okay.
So what happened?
Well, once I was having dinner with my parents and we had a table and on top of the table, there was a glass full of water.
segments.zh: 好吧，有一次我和父母一起吃晚饭，桌子上放着一杯水。

segments.en: And all of a sudden it started to move across the table and then it started to spin while it moved.
segments.zh: 突然间，它开始在桌子上移动，然后在移动时开始旋转。

segments.en: And was there an earthquake or something happening?
segments.zh: 是否发生了地震或发生了什么？

segments.en: No, nothing.
We were just, the only thing on the whole table that was moving was that.
segments.zh: 我们只是，整个桌子上唯一移动的就是那个。

segments.en: And we all just kind of stared at the glass moving and we didn't know what to do.
segments.zh: 我们都只是盯着玻璃移动，我们不知道该怎么办。

segments.en: And then my mom started kind of giggling a nervous laugh and we really didn't know what happened.
segments.zh: 然后我妈妈开始紧张地咯咯笑，我们真的不知道发生了什么。

segments.en: Now, I understand that in Latin America, people are more superstitious.
segments.zh: 现在，我明白在拉丁美洲，人们更加迷信。

segments.en: They believe more in ghosts, right?
Exactly.
In Latin America, people are very superstitious.
segments.zh: 在拉丁美洲，人们非常迷信。

segments.en: They believe in ghosts or in spirits or we have a lot of urban legends about, you know, like a leprechaun that lives under a bridge or, you know, somebody's grandma that comes and haunts them or visits them at night and stuff like that.
segments.zh: 他们相信鬼魂或灵魂，或者我们有很多都市传说，你知道，比如住在桥下的小妖精，或者某人的奶奶晚上回来缠着他们、看望他们之类的。

segments.en: So yeah, Latin American people are very superstitious in this sense.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，从这个意义上说，拉丁美洲人非常迷信。

segments.en: Yeah, I think in Anglo countries, it's a little bit less common to say that you believe in ghosts.
segments.zh: 是的，我觉得在英语国家，说自己相信鬼魂没那么常见。

segments.en: Like maybe inside you, you think ghosts are true, but you wouldn't really tell people that.
segments.zh: 就像你内心一样，你认为鬼魂是真实的，但你不会真正告诉人们。

segments.en: I think the difference would be that you have a different type of superstition.
segments.zh: 我认为不同之处在于你有不同类型的迷信。

segments.en: Like people are afraid of black cats or the floor or the number 13.
segments.zh: 就像人们害怕黑猫或地板或13号一样。

segments.en: Yeah, or opening your umbrella in a house.
segments.zh: 是的，或者在房子里打开你的雨伞。

segments.en: Exactly.
So, because they consider it to be bad luck, but not because something like a ghost or an alien is going to come out and eat them.
segments.zh: 所以，因为他们觉得这代表厄运，而不是因为有什么鬼魂或外星人会出来吃掉他们。
